brief: BofA's strategists argue that investors waiting for a single 'clearing event' to deliver market clarity are mistaken: this year's big IPO, Q3 earnings reactions and recent policy surprises all failed to resolve anything, so the note offers thematic screens for positioning now rather than waiting. On AI, no single driver dominates: capex surprises, capital raises, software disruption and AI-adoption gains among disrupted industries like IT services are all live at once, making AI capex and revenue surprises hard to predict. With AI uncertainty pushing investors toward safe havens, the note flags scarcity: inflation-protected income is scarce as cash real yields stay negative, gold has moved into positive co-movement with stocks since March, and diversification increasingly sits inside the S&P 500 itself via high-dividend and negative-beta stocks. On factors, a value tilt has been working (Value +7% MTD vs Growth -2% and Momentum -5%), led by FCF/EV, though BofA expects GARP to win once profits slow as it forecasts. The note also screens tax-loss candidates that could bounce past the October 31 cutoff and flags potential movers among companies yet to report Q3 earnings.
